item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Read Jay-Z’s Personal Appeal For Lil Durk’s Release
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Jay-Z urges the court to grant Lil Durk bail as Sony pledges financial backing and prosecutors oppose the rapper's release.
item.content:encoded:
Jay-Z urged a federal judge to release Lil Durk on bond, describing an artist who helped young musicians build careers beyond their neighborhoods.

His October 12 letter accompanied a defense filing asking Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald to reconsider Durk’s continued detention.

“I met Durk several years ago. He was kind, respectful and focused on his career. He approached his work with seriousness and discipline. He was also genuinely curious about deepening his spirituality, and he spoke about faith as something he wanted to grow in, not something he wore for show,” Jay-Z explained.

“What stood out most to me was how he used his success. Durk was signing young artists from his community to recording contracts and giving them a real path into a legitimate industry. Many of us come from neighborhoods where the options are limited and the risks are high. Durk understood that, and he worked to help others find a way out of those conditions rather than leaving them behind.”

Durk entered federal custody in October 2024 over accusations he financed a Los Angeles attack targeting Quando Rondo two years earlier.

Prosecutors alleged the August 19, 2022 shooting was retaliation for King Von’s November 2020 killing during a confrontation involving Quando’s associate.

Quando survived the attack, but gunmen killed his cousin Saviay’a Robinson, known as Lul Pab, near the Beverly Center shopping mall.

Jurors returned not-guilty verdicts on all five counts on September 11, 2026, ending the first trial without a conviction against Durk.

Durk remains jailed on separate murder-in-aid-of-racketeering and firearm counts, with prosecutors alleging Only The Family rewarded acts of violence against rivals.

That case includes allegations about Stephon Mack’s January 2022 killing in Chicago; Durk has pleaded not guilty to the pending charges.

Defense lawyer Drew Findling addressed that verdict in the footage below, before Jay-Z’s letter became part of the latest bond application.

“I also note that Durk recently stood trial in this District, and a jury found him not guilty. That verdict deserves weight. He remains presumed innocent of the charges still pending, and I respectfully submit that the jury’s verdict, together with that presumption, supports giving him the opportunity to await trial at home under whatever conditions the Court considers appropriate.”

His lawyers offered future music and branding earnings as security, along with the residence his mother occupies and assets pledged by friends.

Sony Music Entertainment backed a guarantee capped at $1 million, while prosecutors opposed release and Robinson’s family left the decision to the court.

“I do not minimize the seriousness of the charges Durk faces, and I respect the Court’s obligation to protect the community. However, Durk has now spent nearly two years in custody with his remaining trial not set to begin until August 2027. Release would allow him to support his family and continue the work in his community that I saw firsthand.”

item.title: John Legend Earns Music Matters Lifetime Honor
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: John Legend will receive a lifetime achievement award at a 2027 gala raising money to get instruments into more hands.
item.content:encoded:
John Legend will receive a lifetime achievement award at the 2027 Music Matters Awards Gala, with music education at the heart of the celebration.

The Guitar Center Music Foundation will hold the event May 21, 2027, at the Fairmont Century Plaza in Beverly Hills, according to Billboard.

The award recognizes his music, education and philanthropy work. Funds will support instrument grants, and Legend will help a chosen school or nonprofit get instruments. The gala will include dinner, musical tributes and performances, with more honorees and participating artists to be announced.

The singer also made a business move earlier this year. As AllHipHop reported, he joined Roc Nation for management under Jay Brown after leaving Ty Stiklorius’ Friends at Work. Stiklorius continued working with him on other shared business ventures.

The foundation says demand for its help far exceeds what it can provide. It receives more than 150 grant requests each quarter and can meet only about 30 of them.

Founded in 2005, the independent nonprofit says its instrument grants have reached more than 300,000 people through schools and music therapy programs.

Its work reaches beyond schoolchildren. Veterans, hospital patients, unhoused people and people affected by natural disasters are also among those it serves.

One 2024 project shows what that support can look like.

The foundation supplied 16 six-string guitars and two acoustic electric bass guitars for Calle a Calle’s program at A Place Called Home, which serves South Central youth and their families. USC’s Arts in Action initiative funded the program, which taught guitar alongside the social and political context of Corridos Tumbados.

Under the foundation’s grant rules, aid comes as instruments and equipment, with grants valued from $1,000 to $5,000 based on need.

The program serves public schools and U.S. nonprofits that teach people to make music. That includes community classes, after-school instruction and music therapy, with participants of any age eligible.

Programs must have operated for at least a year and offer weekly instruction for at least eight months each year. For now, the foundation says it has paused application reviews while it updates the program and its processes.

item.title: Snoop Dogg Biopic Faced Two Diversity Program Rejections
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Snoop Dogg's biopic faced two diversity program rejections as Universal sought California film incentives, an executive said.
item.content:encoded:
Snoop Dogg‘s biopic faced two rejections in California’s diversity initiative, a Universal executive told the state film commission, according to The Hollywood Reporter.

Universal executive Arturo Barquet discussed the rejections at a June 5 California Film Commission meeting. He said the film later cleared that review. Barquet said he did not know why it had initially been turned away, THR reported.

The commission’s public records list a $17,055,000 credit allocation for the project dated December 8, 2025.

THR reported that final commission approval remained pending, citing a person familiar with the matter.

The state listed the movie as the “Untitled Snoop Dogg Project,” with NBCUniversal as its company. Its entry included 50 California filming days, 84 cast members and 190 crew members, along with $48.3 million in qualified spending.

The diversity rules affect how much of an allocation a production can ultimately claim. Under Program 4.0, a film that does not satisfy the added diversity requirements can qualify for up to 96 percent of its award. The remaining 4 percent depends on documenting its efforts and earning the commission’s approval.

California’s Legislative Analyst’s Office explained that the process involves a workplan, a progress assessment before filming and a final assessment after production. The plans cannot use racial quotas or other numerical goals for protected groups. The review considers whether a production met its goals or made a good-faith effort.

Snoop had publicly thanked the state when its award announcement came in December 2025. He framed the support as a way to make the movie at home.

“Y’all making it possible for us to tell my story right here where it all began,” he said in the state’s announcement.

Universal has set “Snoop” for an August 6, 2027 theatrical release. Jonathan Daviss, known for “Outer Banks,” will play the rapper. Craig Brewer is directing from his rewrite of Joe Robert Cole’s original script.

Snoop is producing alongside Brian Grazer and Death Row Pictures President Sara Ramaker. The movie is the first project under Death Row Pictures’ overall deal with NBCUniversal Entertainment and will use music from his catalog.

Algee Smith has also joined the cast as Warren G, adding another key figure from Snoop’s early career to the film.

item.title: Apple Music Fights Suno Over Private Royalty Details
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Apple Music sought to shield private label deals and royalty terms from Suno's questions in the AI copyright case.
item.content:encoded:
Apple Music asked a judge to stop Suno from questioning it about the streaming business after handing over data on AI songs already reaching listeners.

The dispute put royalty money at the center of the copyright case brought by Universal Music Group and Sony Music against the AI music company.

According to Billboard, Apple said it had answered six document subpoenas from Suno and the labels. That included information on how it finds AI music and how much Suno material appears on its platform.

Apple argued that testimony would expose private business information well beyond what Suno needed, Digital Music News reported. Among the questions: could Apple Music stay in business without the major labels’ catalogs?

Suno also sought details about minimum payments and how royalty terms treated AI songs compared with other music. The demand covered streaming fraud and Apple’s licensing talks with Universal and Sony.

Apple said the companies suing Suno could supply relevant information themselves. It pointed to more than 90 emails and over 10 discussions across more than a year to work out what it would provide.

The labels accused Suno of training on their music without permission and said its AI tracks competed with those recordings. Suno claimed fair use. For artists, that dispute concerns who gets streams and the money attached to them. Warner Music Group, an original plaintiff, settled with Suno in 2025. Universal and Sony’s case continued, with evidence gathering set to last through mid-2027.

Rap producers have a separate stake in the wider fight over AI music. As AllHipHop previously reported, music publisher Reservoir accused Suno of creating tracks that included producer tags, the short signatures heard on rap songs. Reservoir’s lawsuit sought $157.5 million over 1,050 works.

The publisher alleged that Suno trained its tools with songs split into vocals and backing tracks, along with cover versions. Reservoir also sued Anthropic over lyrics, seeking $127.95 million on copyright claims tied to 853 works. Those were separate lawsuits from the Universal and Sony case that brought Apple into the evidence fight.

Apple sought to cancel the testimony demand or obtain an order to protect its information. Digital Music News reported that the motion was listed for December 1, leaving that request for a judge to decide.

item.title: Meek Mill Takes “Dream Chasers Nights” Beyond Philly With Six-City Run
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Meek Mill expanded "Dream Chasers Nights" to six cities, with Boston and Chicago joining the Philadelphia homecoming.
item.content:encoded:
Meek Mill is taking “Dream Chasers Nights” beyond Philadelphia, expanding his hometown concert into a six-city run that stretches from November 24 through December 20.

His official website now lists six cities for the shows. That is a change from the original announcement, which billed the Philadelphia date as a one-night-only homecoming with Live Nation Urban.

The hometown show remains set for November 24 at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Fans outside Philly will also get stops in Boston and Chicago, with Ticketmaster listing December shows in both cities.

Boston’s date is December 5 at MGM Music Hall at Fenway. The show starts at 8 p.m., with doors opening an hour earlier. The event is open to all ages.

Chicago follows on December 18 at Aragon Ballroom, also with a 7 p.m. door time and an 8 p.m. performance. That stop is an all-ages show with general admission standing room.

For Chicago, artist and Citi cardmember presales began October 27 at noon Central time and run through October 29 at 10 p.m. Central. A Live Nation presale starts October 29 at 10 a.m. Central. Those sale times apply to the Chicago date.

The expansion follows another arena show earlier this year. Meek played Total Mortgage Arena in Bridgeport, Connecticut, on April 11 with Fabolous and Young M.A. The concert sold out and grossed $520,526, according to Pollstar’s box-office reporting.

Back home, the Dream Chasers name has reached beyond concert stages. Meek hosted the Dream Chasers Sports and Entertainment Summit for young entrepreneurs at the Liacouras Center in September. His record label carries the name, too.

The Philadelphia date also adds to a year of local appearances. He played Jim Whelan Boardwalk Hall in Atlantic City in June and joined The Roots for a late-night performance at the “One Philly: Unity Concert for America” in July.

His recent music has revisited his early work as well. In July, Meek’s “Nightmares To Dreams” reversed the title of his 2012 song “Dreams And Nightmares.”

Chicago’s general ticket sale opens October 30 at 10 a.m. Central through Ticketmaster. Boston’s general sale starts the same day at 10 a.m. Eastern.

item.title: Neil Young Sues Donald Trump Committee For $10 Million Over Rally Song
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Neil Young sued Donald Trump 47 Committee Inc. for $10 million, alleging his song played at an Ohio rally without permission.
item.content:encoded:
Neil Young sued a Trump political committee for $10 million after he said “Rockin’ in the Free World” played at another rally without his permission. The singer-songwriter filed his copyright lawsuit against Trump 47 Committee Inc. on Monday, October 26, in Virginia federal court, according to Courthouse News Service.

His complaint pointed to the song playing before President Donald Trump took the stage at an October 12 midterm campaign event in Youngstown, Ohio. The committee faced the claim, while Trump was not named as an individual defendant, Rolling Stone reported.

Young also said the dispute carried a cost beyond the use of a recording: he claimed the association hurt his reputation by suggesting he backed Trump, according to TheWrap. His lawyers argued that the message of the song, with its focus on people left behind, conflicted with the politics of the president using it.

“In short, the song is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for,” the filing stated, as quoted by TheWrap.

Young had already taken the Trump campaign to court in 2020 over “Rockin’ in the Free World” and “Devil’s Sidewalk.” That case ended in December 2020 after a settlement that included a promise not to use the song without permission, TheWrap reported.

The new lawsuit alleged the committee lacked the license it needed and had used the song at other events aimed at winning Republican votes in the midterms, Courthouse News Service reported.

The fight over the song stretched back to Trump’s 2015 presidential campaign announcement, when Young publicly objected to its use. He objected again in 2018, Rolling Stone reported, years before the settlement now cited in his latest case.

A separate fight over campaign music reached court in 2024, when the family of R&B great Isaac Hayes challenged Trump’s use of “Hold On, I’m Coming.” Isaac Hayes III announced that a judge had granted an injunction preventing its use at campaign rallies, as AllHipHop reported at the time.

Young’s lawsuit also asked the court to bar the committee from playing any of his songs. Rolling Stone said the White House, the committee and the Republican National Committee did not immediately answer its requests for comment.

item.title: Boosie Badazz Set To Perform With Full Orchestra In Little Rock
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Boosie Badazz brings "The Black Tie Experience" to Little Rock on January 2, with The Signature Orchestra backing his catalog.
item.content:encoded:
Boosie Badazz is taking “The Black Tie Experience” to Little Rock, Arkansas, with a January 2, 2027, date booked at Robinson Center.

The Saturday night show will pair his Southern Hip-Hop catalog with The Signature Orchestra, giving fans a chance to hear his music backed by a live ensemble. The production draws on a recording career that spans more than two decades.

“The Black Tie Experience was created to give audiences a different way to experience Boosie live,” a Stage View Presents spokesperson said in an announcement published by SWARK Today.

Robinson Center’s performance hall seats 2,222. The venue dates to 1939 and underwent a $70 million renovation, according to its website.

For the Little Rock concert, doors are scheduled to open at 7 p.m., an hour before the 8 p.m. show.

The ticket seller limits purchases to nine tickets per person and per credit card. Ticketmaster lists October 23, 2026, as the start of the general sale.

The spokesperson said the production’s size makes touring difficult and limits the number of cities it can reach. Bringing it to Little Rock, the organizer said, would give fans across Arkansas and nearby areas access to the show in a theater setting.

That booking honored Boosie’s Bad Azz and Webbie’s Savage Life, putting the two rappers and those albums at the center of the production. For Dallas, the venue billed a set built around orchestral arrangements of the rappers’ existing work, placing live musicians behind their familiar records.

Another Southern rapper has been taking his catalog into that setting, too. Jeezy announced a second Las Vegas residency, “The Legend Of The Snowman,” an orchestral, black-tie production.

His run at PH Live at Planet Hollywood is set for May and June 2026. While his previous residency focused on Let’s Get It: Thug Motivation 101, the second centered on his broader brand and legacy.

item.title: Nolan Wells March Brings Oxford Students Out For Answers
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nolan Wells' family sought answers as students marched in Oxford and held solidarity events at Rider and Mississippi State.
item.content:encoded:
Nolan Wells‘ name was back on signs at the University of Mississippi on October 25 as students and Oxford residents marched for answers about his death.

University of Mississippi freshmen Christopher Burnett and Avah Trevino organized the event, The Daily Mississippian reported. They walked from Fulton Chapel past the Walk of Champions, the Circle and James Meredith’s statue before returning.

“We just want, simply, for the family’s questions to be answered in further investigation,” Burnett said.

The demand had also reached Rider University, where its NAACP college chapter held an October 22 walk, according to The Rider News.

President E’miija Eccles brought campus Black organizations into the event and contacted Public Safety three weeks ahead. Participants made at least three laps around Centennial Lake.

Founding chapter president Naa’san S.J. Carr, a 2024 graduate, returned to speak. “We gather because remembrance matters, but so does the pursuit of truth and repair,” Carr said.

The marches followed the September 22 Jackson County grand jury decision to bring no criminal charges. Jurors found insufficient evidence to accuse anyone of a crime in the death of the 18-year-old, who had gone to Horn Island with friends for July 4.

Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath said there was no evidence that Wells’ death was racially motivated. Through defense attorney Edward Paltzik, Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo and Morgan Seymour maintained their innocence.

The state autopsy left the cause and manner of his death undetermined, while grand jurors described the circumstances as consistent with drowning.

The Wells family hired civil rights attorney Ben Crump and sought a second autopsy, separate from the state’s examination.

Relatives have said they still want answers about what happened during Wells’ last hours on the island.

At Mississippi State, students rallied on the Drill Field on October 16, The Reflector reported. The Mississippi chapter of the Party for Socialism and Liberation organized it.

NAACP political action co-chair Dave Claggette helped lead the event. Speakers urged students to vote and stay politically involved.

After about an hour, participants held a moment of silence for Wells and Richard E. Holmes, MSU’s first Black student.

item.title: Loe Shimmy Adds Brent Faiyaz To Halloween “Zombieland” Concert
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Loe Shimmy added Brent Faiyaz to his Halloween concert with BigXthaPlug, Sexyy Red and Rob49 at Miramar Amphitheater.
item.content:encoded:
Loe Shimmy is bringing Brent Faiyaz into his Halloween plans, adding the singer to the lineup for his “Zombieland” concert in South Florida.

Faiyaz joins BigXthaPlug, Sexyy Red and Rob49 for the October 31 show at Miramar Regional Park Amphitheater in Miramar, Florida. The concert starts at 8 P.M. Saturday, giving Shimmy a close-to-home stage to bring his rap and R&B collaborators together.

The costumes could pay off, too. A $5,000 cash prize is at stake in the night’s costume contest. The night also includes a haunted house, and Shimmy’s team says the Halloween attractions will include a zombie invasion.

A bigger plan is behind the party.

The venue describes “Zombieland” as the start of Shimmy’s push to build an annual Halloween event. It cites Tyler, The Creator’s Camp Flog Gnaw and Travis Scott’s Astroworld as inspirations for that goal.

The concert’s name also runs through Shimmy’s catalog.

He released Zombieland 2 in March 2024 and expanded it with Zombieland 2.6 that June. The Halloween show turns that recurring theme into a night of music and haunted attractions.

Faiyaz has already been part of Shimmy’s music for years. The pair released “For Me (Remix)” in November 2024, with the track also appearing on Nardy World.

Their partnership continued on “Run The World,” from Shimmy’s Pretty Girlz Run The World. Sexyy Red is on that album as well, joining him on “5 Star Freak.”

For Shimmy, the South Florida show follows the North American tour behind Pretty Girlz Run The World. His team says he recently finished that run, bringing the Halloween date back to the region where he built his name.

AllHipHop was covering the Pompano Beach rapper when he released “Fallin” in 2022. That coverage noted his work with Kodak Black and an early Drake co-sign. Now he’s putting several of his collaborators on the same event bill.

Tickets are available through Ticketmaster. The listing says all ages are welcome and the event will take place rain or shine. Ticket sales are final and nonrefundable.

item.title: French Montana & D-Block Europe’s Copenhagen Concert Is Canceled Too
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: French Montana and D-Block Europe's November 4 Copenhagen concert was canceled, with ticket buyers awaiting more information.
item.content:encoded:
French Montana and D-Block Europe canceled their November 4 show in Copenhagen. The Danish stop joins the other dates fans will miss on their European run.

The rappers were booked to play Store VEGA on Wednesday, November 4. VEGA’s event page now carries a cancellation notice. The venue says ticket buyers will receive more information from the ticket provider. It gives no reason for the cancellation.

The notice does not lay out a refund process for buyers. The page lists a price of 495 Danish kroner, including fees.

Ticketmaster also marks the Copenhagen event as canceled under its listing for the “Worldwide Wave Tour.” The bill paired the British duo with French, the Moroccan-American rapper. They had already made music together.

French appeared on “If I Was Rich Enough” from D-Block Europe’s PTSD 2. They also teamed up on “Fully Loaded,” a collaboration VEGA highlighted when promoting the concert. The planned night paired the duo’s melodic UK rap with French’s American catalog, bringing their studio connection to a shared live bill.

Copenhagen joins two other canceled joint dates AllHipHop previously reported: October 30 at AFAS Live in Amsterdam and November 6 at Raiffeisen Halle im Gasometer in Vienna.

AFAS Live attributed its Amsterdam cancellation to “unforeseen circumstances” and said Ticketmaster would email ticket holders.

VEGA’s notice does not give that explanation for Copenhagen. Ticketmaster’s Vienna listing also labels that concert canceled without explaining why.

D-Block Europe consists of Young Adz and Dirtbike LB. Their third studio album, Rolling Stone, reached No. 1 on the UK’s Official Albums Chart in January 2024, according to Official Charts.

The record-breaking album brought together guests Kodak Black, Yxng Bane and Noizy.

London remains listed separately. Ticketmaster still offers a ticket link for D-Block Europe’s October 28 date at The O2 and includes French Montana in the lineup. For Copenhagen ticket buyers, VEGA directs the next update to the ticket provider.
